description: A sophomore aiming for a career in Data Science who feels strong in mathematical logic but remains cautious about C++ memory management and low-level implementation.

nodes.title: C++ Pointers & References Refresher
nodes.personalizationRationale: Since the student has some_prior_exposure to C++, this node bridges the gap on complex reference and pointer syntax used later in the course.
nodes.description: A focused review of C++ memory semantics, including references and pointer-based array management to solidify foundational understanding.

nodes.title: Advanced C++ OOD & Templates
nodes.personalizationRationale: Given the student's some_prior_exposure, we move directly to core concepts of templates and OOD patterns required for building generic containers.
nodes.description: Introduction to Object-Oriented Design in C++, covering class inheritance, generic programming with templates, and robust error handling via exceptions.

nodes.title: Linked Lists & Algorithm Analysis
nodes.personalizationRationale: Standard core coverage of linked lists and asymptotic analysis, suitable for a student with some_prior_exposure to basic data structures.
nodes.description: Implementation strategies for singly and doubly linked lists, alongside the introduction of asymptotic (Big-O) notation for runtime analysis.

nodes.title: Quiz 1: Recursion & Big-O
nodes.personalizationRationale: First formal check on recursion mastery, essential for all students including those with some_prior_exposure to general programming.
nodes.description: Formal assessment covering recursive algorithm design and the ability to calculate Big-O complexities for linear structures.
Defining and implementing LIFO (Stacks) and FIFO (Queues/Deques) structures using both arrays and linked lists.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core implementation of linear structures, building on the student's some_prior_exposure to programming logic.
nodes.title: Stacks, Queues, and Deques
Vectors, Iterators, and Bubble Sort
nodes.personalizationRationale: Focuses on C++ Standard Library parallels like vectors and iterators, which are highly relevant for a student with some_prior_exposure.
nodes.description: Dynamic array implementations (vectors), iterator patterns for traversal, and the bubble sort algorithm for sequence ordering.
Testing knowledge of stack/queue ADTs and sequence-based algorithm performance.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Assessment of linear data structures to ensure the student with some_prior_exposure is tracking with the cohort.
nodes.title: Quiz 2: Sequence-Based Structures

nodes.personalizationRationale: Mandatory midterm review covering all cumulative content from blocks 01-03 for a student with some_prior_exposure.
nodes.description: Comprehensive review session of all material from C++ foundations through linear data structures in preparation for the midterm.
nodes.title: Midterm Review Session

nodes.personalizationRationale: Core introduction to non-linear structures, assuming the student's some_prior_exposure to basic conditional logic.
nodes.description: Anatomy of general tree structures and binary trees, including depth and height properties.
nodes.title: Tree Fundamentals & Binary Trees
Tree Traversal Algorithms
nodes.personalizationRationale: Exploration of traversal algorithms is a core requirement for the some_prior_exposure tier to master non-linear data flows.
nodes.description: In-depth look at recursive and iterative traversal algorithms: pre-order, post-order, and in-order.

nodes.title: Priority Queues & Heaps
nodes.description: Implementation of priority queues using binary heaps, focusing on the heap-order property and efficient up-heap/down-heap operations.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Efficiency analysis of priority queues and heaps is mandatory core content for students with some_prior_exposure.

nodes.description: Mechanism of hash functions, collision resolution strategies, and skip list structures for efficient searching.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Standard core implementation of hash tables and skip lists for the some_prior_exposure tier.
nodes.title: Maps, Hash Tables, and Skip Lists
Quiz 3: Maps & Hashing
nodes.description: Assessment of hashing efficiency, map ADTs, and the trade-offs between different collision handling methods.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Assessment on hash map mechanics to ensure the student with some_prior_exposure understands effective collision resolution.

nodes.description: Exploring Binary Search Trees and the AVL balancing mechanism to maintain O(log n) performance.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Introduction to balanced search trees is a core required topic for the some_prior_exposure pathway, focusing on tree rotation.
nodes.title: BST & AVL Trees

nodes.description: Detailed analysis of multi-way search trees, (2,4) trees, and the transformation rules for Red-Black trees.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Theoretical grounding in Red-Black and (2,4) trees is a mandatory core requirement for students with some_prior_exposure.
nodes.title: Red-Black & Multi-Way Search Trees
Sorting Algorithms (Merge & Selection)
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core sorting algorithm comparison is a standard requirement for a student with some_prior_exposure to programming.
nodes.description: Comparative study of Merge Sort and Selection Sort, focusing on divide-and-conquer strategies and space complexity.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Final topical quiz ensuring the student with some_prior_exposure has mastered sorting complexities before the final exam.
nodes.description: Final topical quiz focusing on sorting algorithm selection and the integration of multiple data structures in large-scale problems.
nodes.title: Quiz 4: Sorting & Capstone Topics
Cumulative Final Exam Review
nodes.personalizationRationale: Cumulative final review required for all students to demonstrate syllabus-wide proficiency, including those in the some_prior_exposure tier.
nodes.description: Cumulative course review session encompassing the entire syllabus in preparation for the comprehensive final exam.
